headline: product-catalog is intermittently rejecting GetProduct calls (its own span cites a 'Product Catalog Fail Feature Flag'), cascading HTTP 500s into cart, recommendations, product pages, and checkout via frontend. Sustained heavy failure 07:56-08:20 UTC, now tapering in ~5-10 min bursts, most recent burst 08:50 UTC, quiet since.
blast_radius: During active bursts: ~47% of checkout attempts fail (144 failed / 162 ok observed), ~38-47% of product detail page loads fail across all 10 catalog product IDs, and recommendations calls fail at a comparable rate. Cart, product browsing, and purchasing are all degraded because every one of those routes calls product-catalog's GetProduct to hydrate data. Unrelated routes not depending on product-catalog (e.g. /api/data?contextKeys=accessories, ~1.8% failure) are unaffected, so the blast radius is bounded to this one dependency's callers, not system-wide.
reasoning: Single alert, single root cause, so DECLARE rather than ATTACH/MERGE (nothing else is open) or SPLIT (there's only one causal thread here, not two). Chose sev2 over sev1 because the failure is intermittent and self-recovering between bursts rather than a total, unrecovering outage, but it directly hits the revenue-critical checkout path at a high rate during bursts, which rules out sev3/sev4. Status is 'open' rather than 'monitoring' or 'resolved': the most recent burst (08:50 UTC) is only ~7 minutes old at time of writing, and every prior quiet gap of similar length (e.g. 08:23-08:29, 08:41-08:47) was followed by another burst, so a ~7-minute quiet window is not yet evidence of recovery -- it matches the established intermittent pattern, not a break from it.

rca.root_cause: product-catalog's GetProduct gRPC handler is gated by checkProductFailure, which evaluates the OpenFeature/flagd boolean flag productCatalogFailure (default false, generated binding flags.ProductCatalogFailure) per-request via a targetless evaluation context keyed on product_id. When the flag evaluates true for a given request, GetProduct returns before ever calling getProductFromDB, setting a gRPC error with code Internal (13) and the literal message 'Error: Product Catalog Fail Feature Flag Enabled' -- exactly matching the trace evidence (rpc.grpc.status_code=13, grpc.error_message text) verbatim. Because nearly every user-facing route (product detail, cart, recommendations, checkout) calls GetProduct to hydrate product data, this single upstream fault cascades into HTTP 500s across all of them, which is exactly the blast radius alert-grouping observed. This is the demo's deliberate fault-injection code path executing correctly as designed when the flag is on for a given evaluation, not an accidental bug in the flag-check logic itself -- the bursty on/off pattern reflects the flag being toggled/cycled by the fault scenario, not a malfunction in checkProductFailure.
rca.verify_detail: A second, fresh sub-agent, given only the bare claim (file src/product-catalog/main.go, function checkProductFailure, called from GetProduct, gRPC code Internal, literal message 'Error: Product Catalog Fail Feature Flag Enabled', returned before the DB lookup) and no prior reasoning, independently confirmed via `gh api repos/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-demo/contents/src/product-catalog` that the file exists at that path, then fetched the real raw content and quoted: GetProduct calling checkProductFailure at line 373; checkProductFailure at lines 419-420 evaluating flags.ProductCatalogFailure.Value(ctx, openfeature.NewTargetlessEvaluationContext(map[string]any{"product_id": id})); and the error branch at lines 374-377 returning status.Error(codes.Internal, msg) with msg == 'Error: Product Catalog Fail Feature Flag Enabled', with getProductFromDB only reached afterward at line 380. Verdict: CONFIRMED -- every specific element of the claim (path, function, caller, flag reference, error code, exact message, ordering relative to the DB call) is directly and verbatim supported by the real file content, not a plausible-sounding guess.
